description: A curl command that sends one chat request to your local Ollama server and saves the whole response, counts included, to response.json.

steps.description: This `curl` command saves one response from your local Ollama server to `response.json`. The page says you never have to compute a token count, because the model server counts every token it reads and writes and hands you the number.
`curl -s` posts to `http://localhost:11434/api/chat`, Ollama's chat endpoint. The `-s` flag silences progress output. Inside the course container, change `localhost` to `host.docker.internal`.
The request body sets `model` to `llama3.2` and sends one `messages` entry, a user message asking what a token is.
`"stream": false` asks for the whole response in one piece.
The closing `}' > response.json` redirects the response into the file `response.json`.

steps.question: The page says with streaming on, the counts arrive only in the last chunk, the one with which flag set to true?

title: Saving One Ollama Response
